summary: STAAR Hub iteration 6 — FRONTEND ONLY web-audio-fix verification at 390x844. CORE FIX VERIFIED: All 4 exercised cinematic/ambient MP3s now stream successfully from /audio/*.mp3 with HTTP 206 Partial Content and content-type audio/mpeg (previously failed to resolve on web). Files confirmed: toronto-portal.mp3 (traverse cue on cinematic mount), transition.mp3 (on SKIP CINEMATIC), hub.mp3 (on PLAY HUB AMBIENCE), shield.mp3 (during phase transitions). curl https://cross-life-ai.preview.emergentagent.com/audio/opening.mp3 → HTTP 200 audio/mpeg (60,858 bytes). PARTIAL on 'zero pageerrors' criterion: after ENABLE SOUND click loading the FIRST cue, zero 'no supported source' pageerrors fire — the initial cue that previously failed is now clean. However, 3 errors fire on SKIP CINEMATIC (new cue replaces old) and 2 more on PLAY HUB AMBIENCE toggle (~5 per scoped test, ~35 over full session vs. previously 57). Root cause: expo-audio web player teardown — cueRef.current?.remove() in /app/frontend/lib/staarwardd/audio-provider.tsx clears the underlying HTMLAudioElement's src before disposal, which fires an 'error' event on the OLD element even though the NEW player loads the new source successfully with 206. This is COSMETIC (playback works, files stream, buttons toggle) but does not meet the strict 'zero pageerrors' bar. Regression suite 100% pass: (a) fresh session cinematic shows TORONTO RESPONSE FLIGHT + ENABLE SOUND + SKIP CINEMATIC; (b) ENABLE SOUND flips to SOUND ON; (c) SKIP → hub with STAAR COMMAND ENVIRONMENT; (d) PLAY HUB AMBIENCE toggles to STOP HUB AMBIENCE and back; (e) AWAKEN THE GATEWAYS reveals all 7 portals (Creativity, Work, Home, Wellbeing, Relationships, Events, Style); (f) Work portal opens /portal/work → EXECUTIVE COMMAND WORKSPACE; (g) direct /hub renders STAAR COMMAND ENVIRONMENT. Also observed 1x 'play() interrupted by pause()' pageerror (benign race between remove/play in playCue). Deprecation warnings persist (carry-over from iter 4-5): shadow*, textShadow*, pointerEvents prop, useNativeDriver.

integration_issues.flow: Cinematic audio cue teardown on web
integration_issues.issue: When a new cinematic cue plays (transition on SKIP, subsequent cues) or when playCue is called with an existing cueRef, the old HTMLAudioElement is removed via player.remove() which triggers a 'no supported source' MediaError on the outgoing element even though the incoming cue's mp3 loads successfully (206 audio/mpeg). Net effect: ~5 residual pageerrors during a scoped click flow (~35 during full session traversal), down from 57 pre-fix. Non-blocking — all audio playback works, network confirms streaming. Reference: /app/frontend/lib/staarwardd/audio-provider.tsx:104-142 (playCue / toggleAmbient / stopAll each call player.remove()). Suggested fix: before player.remove(), attach a one-time 'error' event handler that swallows MEDIA_ERR_SRC_NOT_SUPPORTED on teardown, or wrap the entire cinematic audio path in an installErrorSuppressor() on web only (Platform.OS === 'web') using window.addEventListener('error', suppressAudioSrcErrors, true).

1x pageerror captured: 'The play() request was interrupted by a call to pause()' — occurs when playCue replaces an existing player mid-load. Cosmetic; audio still plays. Reference: /app/frontend/lib/staarwardd/audio-provider.tsx:132-142.

react_native_issues.issue: Console warnings persist: '"shadow*" style props are deprecated. Use "boxShadow"', '"textShadow*" style props are deprecated. Use "textShadow"', 'props.pointerEvents is deprecated. Use style.pointerEvents', 'Animated: useNativeDriver is not supported... Falling back to JS-based animation'. Reference: hub-adjacent components. Non-blocking.

action_items: Suppress the residual 'no supported source' pageerrors from expo-audio's HTMLAudioElement teardown on web. Recommended approach in /app/frontend/lib/staarwardd/audio-provider.tsx: (1) On web only, before calling `player.remove()`, first do `player.pause()` and then swallow the resulting MediaError. Alternative: install a global one-shot capture-phase listener in the provider mount effect that suppresses `error` events whose target is an HTMLAudioElement with src pointing at /audio/*.mp3 (indicates teardown noise, not a real failure). This is what will get pageerror count to zero.
(Optional) Address the 'play() interrupted by pause()' race in playCue by awaiting the previous player's play() promise (or checking a ready state) before calling .remove() on the previous cueRef.
(Carry-over from iter 5) Migrate deprecated shadow*/textShadow*/pointerEvents props in hub-adjacent components to silence RN-Web deprecation warnings.
critical_code_review_comments: /app/frontend/lib/staarwardd/audio-provider.tsx correctly branches on Platform.OS === 'web' to use { uri: '/audio/<name>.mp3' } sources — verified toronto-portal.mp3, transition.mp3, hub.mp3, shield.mp3 all return 206 audio/mpeg from the public folder. The fix strategy is sound and the mapping table matches file names in /app/frontend/public/audio/.

The teardown pattern (cueRef.current?.remove() followed by createAudioPlayer(...)) at lines 120-125 and 136-140 is the ROOT CAUSE of the remaining pageerrors. On web, expo-audio wraps an HTMLAudioElement which fires an MediaError event when src is cleared during dispose. Consider adding an error-suppression shim for web only.
Constraint honored: no changes to /app/frontend/index.js, components/staarwardd/*, or package.json 'main'. tsc --noEmit not re-run this iteration (no code changes made).

/app/frontend/public/audio/ contains all 16 expected mp3s and served with correct audio/mpeg + accept-ranges: bytes (curl verified). CORS headers present. Preview host correctly proxies /audio/ to the Expo static output.

success_rate.frontend: 6.5/7 review checks pass — audio streaming fix works (200/206 audio/mpeg confirmed for toronto-portal, transition, hub, shield); regression 100% (portals, Work, /hub); curl check passes; the 'zero no-supported-source pageerrors' criterion is PARTIALLY met (0 on initial ENABLE SOUND cue; ~5 during subsequent cue transitions, ~35 across full session vs. 57 previously).

context_for_next_testing_agent: IMPORTANT MEASUREMENT NOTE: Do NOT use page.on('requestfinished') for streamed media (206 Partial Content). Playwright's requestfinished does NOT fire for streaming media requests. Use page.on('request') + page.on('response') instead to reliably count /audio/*.mp3 fetches. Confirmed audio files served with 206 audio/mpeg: toronto-portal.mp3, transition.mp3, hub.mp3, shield.mp3 (and opening.mp3 via direct fetch 200). Timeline: ENABLE SOUND triggers traverse cue (toronto-portal.mp3, immediate on cinematic mount phase change). SKIP CINEMATIC triggers transition.mp3 via audio.playCue('transition') in leave() callback. PLAY HUB AMBIENCE fetches hub.mp3 via toggleAmbient('hub'). Residual 'no supported source' pageerrors come from cueRef.current?.remove() teardown, NOT from source loading (network confirms all loads succeed). For clean zero-pageerror verification post-fix, capture pageerror count DELTAS around each interaction; the first cue after mount should still be 0, subsequent cue swaps are where the noise originates. Frontend URL: https://cross-life-ai.preview.emergentagent.com. Fresh session recipe: goto /, run `localStorage.clear(); sessionStorage.clear();`, goto / again, wait 3000ms, then click ENABLE SOUND (force=True) via `page.get_by_text('ENABLE SOUND', exact=True)`. SKIP button visible ~620ms after mount.
rca_of_issue: Bug: Guardian cinematic sound cues fired 'Failed to load because no supported source was found' 57 times on web. Applied fix (in /app/frontend/lib/staarwardd/audio-provider.tsx) switches source declarations from bundled require() assets to { uri: '/audio/<name>.mp3' } when Platform.OS === 'web', with the mp3 files staged at /app/frontend/public/audio/ and served with audio/mpeg MIME. Verification confirms: (a) the underlying playback failure is RESOLVED — every cue whose source is exercised streams successfully (HTTP 206 audio/mpeg for toronto-portal, transition, hub, shield; HTTP 200 for opening via direct fetch); (b) the residual ~35 'no supported source' pageerrors have a DIFFERENT root cause than the original bug — they now come from the teardown side of the cue swap in audio-provider.tsx (player.remove() clears the HTMLAudioElement src, which fires an error on the discarded element even though the new player loads fine). Reproduction: click ENABLE SOUND (0 err), then SKIP CINEMATIC (+3 err), then PLAY HUB AMBIENCE (+2 err). Mitigation: install a web-only error suppressor that swallows MEDIA_ERR_SRC_NOT_SUPPORTED on HTMLAudioElements pointing at /audio/*.mp3 during teardown, or pause the outgoing player before calling remove() and detach its src cleanly.
